title: Order.additionalFees: What does this actually contain? Duties on order but still empty
text: Hi, I am an integrator that listens to the orders/create webhook, fetches the order via the GraphQL Admin API (read_orders) in order to create invoices in our own system. For that we need every customer-facing charge. The API docs claim about additionalFees: “Additional fees applied to an Order beyond the standard product and shipping costs.” In practice I have observed that the field doesn’t behave that way and I could not find any reliable information about that either. What the docs promise: AdditionalFee: “Additional fees applied to an Order beyond the standard product and shipping costs. Additional fees typically include duties, import fees, or other special handling charges that need separate tracking from regular LineItem objects.” Order.additionalFees: “A list of additional fees applied to an order, such as duties, import fees, or tax lines.” What I actually observed: In an order created via normal checkout where duties were applied (…TotalDutiesSet wer non-zero as well as the duties field for specific lineItems) the additionalFees field returns an empty list. This contradicts the description of the field in the docs. This leads to following questions: What concretely populates Order.additionalFees? What is in there and under which conditions? Can someone confirm that duties always are in the lineItems and never in additionalFees? Would, if set, originalTotalAdditionalFeesSet / currentTotalAdditionalFeesSet include duties? If additionalFees is not the catch-all we hoped for: what is the authoritative, complete set of customer-facing charges? lineItems (+ taxLines) + shippingLines (+ taxLines) + lineItems.duties + ??? What fields are missing here to always cover all customer facing charges? Could duties be double-counted if they were present in additionalFees (if it is in there under some nebulous conditions) I.e. duties that are listed in additionalFields are not in lineItems duties? Thank you for any help and information. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic

triage_reason: Order.additionalFees field is empty despite duties being present on order.

title: Closed for the holidays? Your local pickup ready time has no idea
text: If you offer local pickup, the only timing Shopify knows about is the processing time on each location (Settings, Shipping and delivery, Pickup in store, click the location, Expected pickup date). It’s a fixed list that runs from one hour up to five days or more, and whatever you picked is what customers see at checkout and, on themes that support it, on the product page. I couldn’t find anything in those settings or the help docs for opening hours, closed days or holidays, so a “usually ready in 2 hours” promise keeps running on Thanksgiving morning exactly like it does on a normal Tuesday. The two minute check is to open that location’s pickup settings, read the processing time you chose back when you set it up, and ask whether it’s still true for an order placed the evening before your longest closure this season. If it isn’t, there are a couple of native levers. You can switch it to the two to four day or five days or more option for the holiday stretch, or turn pickup off for that location while you’re shut so it simply isn’t offered at checkout. Your pickup instructions for the location also go into the ready for pickup email, which is a decent place for holiday hours, though it only reaches people once their order is ready. Neither lever lets a customer choose the day they’ll come in, and as far as I can see neither one can be scheduled, so whatever you change stays changed until you change it back. Worth a calendar reminder for the morning you reopen. 5 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
author: dropfeed
triage_reason: Local pickup processing time settings do not support holiday hours/scheduling.

title: Shopify issue 0 atc website not working right
text: Hi everyone, I’m experiencing a serious issue with my Shopify store, and I’ve been trying to solve it for approximately three weeks. I’m running Meta (Facebook/Instagram) ads targeting mainly UK customers and sending visitors directly to three product landing pages. The main problem: My store receives traffic, but almost nobody interacts with the website. For example, yesterday I received approximately 200 visitors with 0 add-to-carts . What I’m experiencing Visitors arrive from Meta ads but leave after only a few seconds. Microsoft Clarity recordings often show visitors staying at the top of the landing page without scrolling or clicking. Some recordings appear frozen, with white/grey screens or images that don’t load correctly. Occasionally, the page seems difficult to scroll or interact with. Some visitors appear to experience layout shifting. Product images and galleries sometimes seem slow to load. Shopify, Meta and Microsoft Clarity report inconsistent traffic and behavioral data. Almost no add-to-cart activity is recorded from real customers, despite continuous paid traffic. What I’ve already tried Over the past two weeks, I’ve: Optimized product images, videos and loading priorities. Tested different Shopify theme versions, including cleaner versions with apps disabled. Investigated third-party scripts, leftover app code and duplicated JavaScript. Checked potential conflicts involving Klaviyo, Microsoft Clarity, Triple Whale and Shopify Forms. Investigated tracking, cookies and Shopify’s Customer Privacy settings. Tested the landing pages using Google PageSpeed Insights and mobile performance tests. Investigated issues with the sticky add-to-cart button, image gallery and scrolling behavior. Compared recordings from UK visitors with my own test sessions. Investigated whether Meta’s in-app browser behaves differently from normal browsers. I’ve contacted the Shopify, Meta, Microsoft Clarity, and Klaviyo support teams, but the issue remains unresolved. I’m still in contact with Shopify Support to resolve this issue. Despite these changes, the problem persists. Important details My store uses a customized Shopify theme with three separate product landing pages. Most paid traffic comes from Meta ads targeting the UK. The website has undergone many code modifications and theme optimizations. I previously moved the store to a different Shopify account while retaining the same domain, theme and Meta pixel. Some analytics sessions are my own tests, so I’m mainly concerned about real UK customer behavior. My biggest concern is that visitors may be experiencing a technical issue that prevents them from browsing or interacting normally. What I’m trying to figure out Could this problem be caused by: A JavaScript error or conflicting scripts preventing interactions? Shopify app code that remains in the theme after uninstalling apps? A problem specifically affecting Meta’s in-app browser? Images, overlays or sticky elements blocking touch interactions? Shopify consent settings interfering with analytics and making visitors appear inactive? A theme performance issue that doesn’t show up consistently in PageSpeed Insights? My main question: Has anyone experienced a Shopify store receiving hundreds of Meta ad visitors but almost zero add-to-carts, while session recordings show visitors appearing frozen or leaving without scrolling? I want to determine whether customers genuinely aren’t interested or whether something is preventing them from using the website properly. Any suggestions for debugging this would be greatly appreciated. Thanks in advance! 6 posts - 3 participants Read full topic
author: Mg076
triage_reason: Shopify store receiving traffic and zero add-to-carts due to potential website break.
